note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right wrist and hand pain, numbness, and tingling in fingers

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a landscaper presenting with several months of right wrist and hand pain associated with numbness and tingling in the fingers. Symptoms are most noticeable at night, with patient experiencing paresthesias that wake him from sleep and require shaking out his hand for relief. He notes numbness predominantly in the thumb and pointer finger but also involving the fifth finger at times. The left hand has not been affected. Patient denies knowledge of inciting event; symptoms began insidiously. Occupational history significant for landscaping work involving repetitive heavy labor including raking and digging. Patient notes associated weakness in the left hand with difficulty gripping objects and dropping items due to sensory loss.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports numbness and tingling in bilateral fingers with associated weakness. Denies right hand involvement. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history reported. Patient denies history of rheumatoid arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
None reported

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in landscaping, performing yard work and maintenance. Heavy labor with repetitive motions. Alcohol use: one to two beers on weekends (Fridays and Saturdays).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm
General: alert and oriented
Strength: grip strength reduced on left compared to right
Sensory: intact bilaterally; patient notes sensation feels slightly different on thumb side versus pointer finger side
Neurological exam: Tinel's sign positive bilaterally at wrist

RESULTS
Bilateral positive Tinel's sign

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, likely related to repetitive occupational activities. Plan: (1) Order EMG study to measure electrical impulses in fingers; (2) Activity modification—patient to delegate heavy repetitive work to employees for several weeks; (3) Wrist splint to wear; (4) Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours; (5) Follow-up office visit in 2 weeks to reassess and determine need for further diagnostic testing or possible surgical intervention for nerve decompression.
